newsitem.title: USA: FDA panel backs Hologic BMD device.
newsitem.headline: FDA panel backs Hologic BMD device.

text.p: A U.S. Food and Drug Administration advisory panel on Monday voted unanimously to approve, with conditions, Hologic Inc.'s Sahara ultrasound device, used to estimate bone mineral density.
The panel said that Hologic needs to include more information in its labeling on usage by men and non-white females, and better physician and patient education about when to use the device.
The FDA is not bound by its panels' advice, but usually follows it.

BMD strongly predicts the risk for osteoporosis, estimated to affect at least 23 million American, primarily white, women. Osteoporosis costs the country $14 billion a year, which includes drug therapies and hospitalization for fractures.

Hologic claimed that Sahara is as clinically useful and cheaper, safer and more accessible than dual X-ray absorptionetry (DXA). But the panel said that Sahara can only be used to "predict" results of DXA, which may curb enthusiasm for the device.
Hologic has said that Sahara, a $30,000, 20-pound device, may increase access to screening and therefore treatment.
